overview.text: The South American Rattlesnake is a highly venomous pit viper and the most widespread rattlesnake of all.

identification.text: Two stripes run back from the base of the head; the body pattern varies, usually with a row of dark diamonds. A rattle on the tail.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 1.5 m long, rarely up to 1.9 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Much of South America: Colombia, Venezuela, the Guianas, Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay and northern Argentina, and Aruba.

behaviour.text: Most active at dusk and early morning. It gives little warning before striking, but like other rattlesnakes it is seldom aggressive to people.

reproduction.text: Males compete for females at the end of summer, mating happens in autumn and the live young are born the next spring or summer.
